metaDescription: HEPA upright vacuums compared by sealed housings, bagged versus bagless design and emptying hygiene, so the filter actually keeps fine dust out of your air.
expertTake: The Kenmore Elite 31150 is the strongest allergy pick here because it pairs bagged collection with triple HEPA and a beltless two-motor nozzle. The Shark ZU561 is the best bagless option with a published complete seal. Skip any model that only says HEPA on the box; the label means little without a sealed housing.
introParagraphs: A HEPA filter is only as good as the path the air takes to reach it. If the housing leaks at the seams, fine dust bypasses the filter and comes out of the exhaust, which is why two vacuums with the same label can behave very differently in a room with an allergy sufferer.

The useful questions are whether the housing is sealed, whether dust is collected in a bag or a cup, and how you empty it. A bagged machine contains dust until the bag is thrown away, while a bagless one releases a puff each time the cup is opened.

products.name: Kenmore Elite 31150 bagged upright, triple HEPA, beltless

specList.label: Filtration
specList.value: HEPA, traps 99.97 percent down to 0.3 microns

specList.label: Motors
specList.value: Two nozzle motors plus an Inducer Motor

products.description:
A bag changes the dust story: dirt goes into a closed bag that you throw away whole, so the fine particles that are most irritating to allergy sufferers never get a chance to puff into the room. The Elite pairs that with HEPA filtration the maker rates at 99.97 percent of dust down to 0.3 microns and a design in which two motors sit in the nozzle, with no belts to change, plus an Inducer Motor for suction.

Next to the Shark ZU561 it relies on a bag rather than a sealed bagless cup, and the beltless design removes the most common repair. The trade is that bags are a recurring cost, and a bag that packs solid cuts airflow, so you replace it before it looks full.

Watch the bag more than anything: change it when it is about two thirds full, check that it seats flat against the intake, and never run the machine with the bag door unlatched. Replace the HEPA filter on the schedule in the manual, because a loaded filter strains the Inducer Motor. Keep a pack of spare bags with the vacuum so you never fall back on running it bagless. Because the nozzle holds two small motors, never tip the machine back while the brushes are still spinning, and let the head rest flat when you pause, since a nozzle that gets knocked sideways can stress the wiring that carries power to the brush motors. When the bag door closes, listen for the latch, because a bag door that sits slightly open breaks the seal that justifies buying this model.
products.bestFor: Allergy households that want bagged containment and a low-maintenance drive.
pros: HEPA filtration claim of 99.97 percent at 0.3 microns
cons: Filter must be replaced on schedule

products.name: Shark ZU561 Navigator Lift-Away Speed with complete seal

specList.label: Filtration
specList.value: HEPA, over 99.9 percent of dust and allergens

products.description:
Shark's anti-allergen complete seal is the clearest statement of a sealed housing among the bagless models: the system is built so the air passes through the HEPA filter rather than around it, and the maker rates the combination at over 99.9 percent of dust and allergens. A self-cleaning brushroll deals with pet hair, and the pod detaches for stairs and furniture.

Compared with the Kenmore Elite it uses a cup rather than a bag, so it is cheaper to run but releases some dust at emptying. The seal depends on rubber gaskets, so the model rewards owners who check them.

Empty the cup outdoors into a bag held tight to the opening, and wash the foam and felt filters when the maker says. Look at the gaskets every few months for cracks, since a hardened seal is the first thing to fail on a sealed machine, and replace the HEPA filter on schedule so the system is not strained. If you have a pet that sheds heavily, expect the pre-filter foam to load faster than the manual implies, and wash it every few weeks instead of monthly, drying it completely before it goes back, because a damp foam filter in a sealed housing can grow a musty smell that the motor then spreads around the room.
products.bestFor: Allergy homes that prefer a bagless machine with a stated seal.
pros: Complete seal around the HEPA filter
cons: Bagless cup releases dust when emptied

products.name: Oreck HEPA bagged upright with two-speed brush roll

specList.label: Capacity
specList.value: Holds up to 4X more than a standard bagless

products.description:
Oreck's approach is a light, bagged upright with HEPA media filtration and a two-speed brush roll, so you can slow the roll for hardwood and tile and speed it up for carpet. The bag holds, the maker says, up to four times more debris than a standard bagless cup, which cuts the number of times the dust is handled.

Beside the Elite it is lighter and simpler, but it has a single motor and a belt-driven roll. For an allergy household that also wants to carry the machine up stairs, that is the trade.

Change the bag when it is about two thirds full, check the belt every few months and keep the HEPA media on its schedule. A light machine tips easily, so park it standing, and avoid vacuuming wet or very fine powders such as drywall dust, which clog a HEPA filter in minutes. The two-speed roll is a small but real help for allergy households, because a slower roll on hard floors flicks less dust into the air than a fast one, and the bag's larger capacity means you change it less often than a cup would need emptying. Keep a few spare bags and a spare belt in a zip bag taped to the closet wall so that a worn part does not push you back to an old vacuum.
products.bestFor: Allergy homes that want a light, bagged HEPA upright.
pros: Two-speed brush roll for floor types
cons: Belt-driven roll needs a belt change

products.name: Bissell CleanView Max Allergen 4377, MicroCAPTURE sealed
products.description:
This Bissell leads with a sealed system and says its MicroCAPTURE design plus HEPA filtration captures and holds 99.97 percent of dust. A tangle-free brush roll aimed at pets is the second selling point, which makes it relevant for homes where dander and hair arrive together.

It is a bagless design, so it releases dust at emptying like the Shark, and the capture figure is a maker claim. Next to the Shark ZU561 it offers a similar sealed idea without the lift-away pod.

Empty the tank outdoors, rinse the washable filter on schedule and let it dry for a full day. Inspect the seal around the tank for debris, since a pebble in the gasket leaves a gap that lets fine dust bypass the filter, and check the brush roll for hair at the ends. A sealed bagless machine is only as good as the way you empty it, so carry the tank to the outdoor bin, hold a bag tight around the opening and release the latch slowly, letting the contents drop rather than shaking them out, and rinse the tank only if the maker says it is washable, since moisture left in a closed tank can create a smell that lingers.
products.bestFor: Pet households that want a sealed system with a tangle-free roll.
cons: Capture figure is a maker claim

products.name: Kenmore Intuition bagged lift-up upright, sealed HEPA

specList.label: Seal
specList.value: HEPA with a completely sealed system

specList.label: Emptying
specList.value: Press to release the full bag

products.description:
The Intuition is the Kenmore that removes the messiest step. A single button press releases a full bag, so you never touch the dirt, and a lift-up pod gives you a lightweight unit for stairs and above-floor cleaning. HEPA filtration and a completely sealed system trap 99.97 percent of dust inside the vacuum, according to the maker.

Compared with the Elite it is lighter and cheaper, with a pod rather than a beltless nozzle. A home with stairs and an allergy sufferer is the natural match.

Check that the bag seats properly each time, because a bag that is not latched can leak into the housing, and buy spare bags in the right size. The lift-up pod has a joint that holds the seal, so wipe it monthly and rinse any washable filter on schedule. Because the pod detaches, make a habit of reattaching it with a firm press until it clicks before you start the motor, since a pod that is only resting in place leaks air at the joint and turns a sealed system into an ordinary one without any visible sign, apart from a slightly different motor sound and weaker suction on the floor.
products.bestFor: Allergy homes with stairs that want bagged containment.
pros: Press-to-release bag keeps your hands clean
cons: Pod joint is an extra seal
Capture figure is a maker claim

products.name: Prolux Phantom Pro commercial bagged upright, HEPA
products.description:
The Phantom Pro is a commercial bagged upright that adds HEPA filtration and attachments, which many commercial machines skip. It leans on the bagged argument that bags give more suction than cups for deep cleaning, a claim from the maker.

It is a heavier, more rugged option than the home models, and a good choice for a home with an allergy sufferer that wants a durable machine rather than a plastic one. Next to the Kenmore Elite it is simpler and more serviceable, but it lacks the beltless nozzle.

Replace the bag at two thirds full, check the belt and brush, and replace the HEPA filter on schedule. A commercial design is easy to repair, so keep a spare belt and a few bags in the closet. A commercial design is also less likely to crack when dropped on a stair, which is a real advantage over thin plastic home uprights, but it is heavier to carry, so it suits a house where the vacuum lives on one floor. Check that the HEPA filter fits snugly in its housing after each replacement, because a filter that sits askew lets air go around it.
products.bestFor: Allergy homes that want a rugged commercial machine with HEPA.
cons: Belt-driven roll needs a belt change

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Shark ZU561 advertises an anti-allergen complete seal, the Bissell 4377 a MicroCAPTURE sealed system and the Kenmore Intuition a completely sealed system. A HEPA filter in a leaky housing lets fine dust bypass it. Look for the seal statement, not just the word HEPA, and treat a listing that says nothing about sealing as a regular vacuum with a good filter, because the cost of a sealed design is in gaskets and molded joints that a manufacturer will mention if they exist.

The Kenmore Elite, Oreck and Prolux use bags, which contain dust until you throw the bag away. The Shark and Bissell use cups, which release a puff when opened. For severe allergies, a bag is the better path, and the cost of bags, which is real but modest, is the price of keeping the dust contained, so budget for a year of bags when you compare the running cost of a bagged model with a bagless one.
The Kenmore Intuition releases a full bag with one press. A bagless cup should be emptied outdoors into a bag held tight to the opening. How you empty matters as much as the filter.

HEPA filters are wear parts. The Kenmore Elite and Oreck specify a schedule, and a loaded filter strains the motor. Check the price and availability of the replacement before you buy, and favor a model whose filter is sold by several shops, because a filter that exists only through one seller can disappear and leave you with a vacuum that cannot be run safely.

An upright is heavy to carry. The Shark ZU561 and Kenmore Intuition have lift-away or lift-up pods for stairs, and the Oreck is light. Match the weight to your home, and consider whether a second, lighter machine for the upstairs would let you keep a heavier sealed unit on the ground floor, which is where most of the dust that bothers allergy sufferers actually collects.

Capture figures such as 99.97 percent and 99.9 percent are the makers' numbers, measured by their own methods. They are a sign of design intent, not a guarantee in your room. Look for the seal and the bag, not just the percentage.

cards.label: Bagged
cards.text: The Kenmore Elite, Intuition, Oreck and Prolux contain dust in a bag. Bags cost money, and a packed bag cuts airflow.

cards.label: Bagless
cards.text: The Shark ZU561 and Bissell 4377 use cups. They are cheaper to run but release dust when emptied.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A sealed housing, a roll that resists hair wrap and a way to empty without a cloud. Wash or replace filters on schedule.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Shark ZU561 has a self-cleaning roll and a seal, and the Bissell 4377 adds a tangle-free roll with a sealed system.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Anyone in the home has asthma or serious allergies. The Kenmore Elite's bag and triple HEPA are worth it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Allergies are mild. The Shark ZU561 gives a stated seal at a lower tier.

faq.q: Is a bagless HEPA vacuum okay?
faq.a: If it has a complete seal, yes, but empty the cup outdoors.

faq.q: Do HEPA vacuums need special bags?
faq.a: Use the bags made for the model. Wrong bags can leak and void the sealed design.
